title: URL-and-ID-edgecases-labeling-notebook
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for how we should label weird URL/ID-like tokens in the user text corpus. Goal is a compact set of heuristics and example mappings labelers can follow in the first-pass labeling round. This is a scratchpad — lots of TODOs and open q's below.

Summary of the problem:
- Our corpus contains many short, truncated, or obfuscated tokens that *look like* URLs/IDs but are not canonical (examples: t.co/abc, user:12345, abc.def, 2020-12-31-121314, /u/xyz, snippet@service).
- Labelers are inconsistent: some mark as URL, others mark as CODE_SNIPPET or PERSON_ID; downstream models treat these inconsistently and we get precision drop on PII detection and retrieval.

Proposal (high-level):
- Primary labels: URL, EMAIL, USER_ID, ORDER_ID, TIMESTAMP, CODE_SNIPPET, NOISE, OTHER_ID, UNKNOWN.
- When in doubt between URL vs NOISE, mark URL if token contains any valid scheme (http, https, ftp) OR a domain-like tld (dot + 2-6 letters) AND at least one slash or dot-separated path fragment.
- If token is well-formed but truncated (ends with ellipses or a line-break mid-token), label as URL_TRUNCATED? (we might combine with OTHER_ID rather than add label complexity).

Concrete heuristics for labelers (working):
1) URL (include short links):
   - Contains scheme: http://, https://, ftp:// => URL
   - Starts with www. and then a domain => URL
   - Short redirect domains (t.co, bit.ly, goo.gl) + slash + alphanum => URL (even if path is short)
   - tokens like example.com/path, sub.domain.co.uk, domain.io?q=1 => URL
   - If token contains a dot followed by a 2-6 letter suffix and has a slash or query string, prefer URL

2) EMAIL:
   - contains @ and domain-like tail => EMAIL (unless it's noisy like @username inside social text where context indicates a handle — see USER_HANDLE below)

3) USER_HANDLE / USER_ID (separate):
   - Social handles: @username, /u/username => USER_HANDLE (not EMAIL)
   - Patterns: user_id=12345, uid:12345, id: 0x1a2b => USER_ID if context points to account identifiers
   - If the numeric token is long (>8 digits) and preceded by invoice|order|txn|order_id => ORDER_ID

4) NUMERIC IDENTIFIERS vs TIMESTAMP:
   - 10+ digits that look like epoch seconds (>= 1e9) -> TIMESTAMP if context temporal
   - yyyy-mm-dd | yyyy/mm/dd | yyyy.mm.dd optionally with time => TIMESTAMP
   - compact date-time formats (20201231T123000) -> TIMESTAMP

5) CODE_SNIPPET / PATHS:
   - tokens containing file extensions and slashes without tld (e.g., /usr/bin/python, ./src/main.py) -> CODE_SNIPPET or FILE_PATH
   - tokens with punctuation typical of code ({}, =>, def(), ; ) -> CODE_SNIPPET

6) OTHER_ID / NOISE:
   - short alphanumeric tokens used as internal references (abc123) with no context -> OTHER_ID or NOISE depending on downstream risk. Prefer OTHER_ID if used in product logs or support transcripts.
   - tokens with many punctuation noise (***, ---, ####) => NOISE

7) Ambiguity rules / tie-breakers:
   - If a token contains both @ and a dot e.g., "@company.com" in slack mention, use context: if prefix is @ and rest is domain -> USER_HANDLE if used as a mention; EMAIL if clearly used as address ("email me at ...").
   - If token looks like domain but is missing tld ("example/path"), prefer URL if there is a slash and it looks like a path.
   - If token is super short (<4 chars) and only alnum ("a1b2"), prefer NOISE unless surrounding text references account numbers.

Examples (annotate = label):
- "https://t.co/xYz12" => URL
- "t.co/xYz12" => URL (short link)
- "Please send to john.doe@example.com" => EMAIL
- "@john.doe posted" => USER_HANDLE
- "order_id=987654321" => ORDER_ID
- "txn:0x7af3b" => USER_ID or OTHER_ID (service-specific hex) -> USER_ID if logs mention account; else OTHER_ID
- "2021-09-01T12:01:05Z" => TIMESTAMP
- "file: ./app/main.py" => FILE_PATH / CODE_SNIPPET
- "invoice # 12345" => ORDER_ID
- "abc.xyz" (isolated) => UNKNOWN / flag for review (could be product slug or malformed domain)

Sampling plan for review: 
- Pull 2k random tokens that match regex: [a-zA-Z0-9\-_.:/@]{6,} and present in labeled dataset. Manually review 500 for disagreement analysis.
- Stratify by source: support chats, error logs, scraped forums; expect different distributions.

Labeler checklist (quick):
- Is there a scheme (http, ftp)? -> URL
- Is there an @ with domain? -> EMAIL unless clearly mention-style -> USER_HANDLE
- Is it prefixed with invoice/order/txn? -> ORDER_ID
- Is it a path (starts with / or ./ or contains file extension)? -> FILE_PATH/CODE_SNIPPET
- If still unsure -> add comment flag_for_review and pick OTHER_ID

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a separate URL_TRUNCATED label? Pros: explicit signal for downstream cropping. Cons: extra label complexity for labelers.
- Should short redirect domains always be labeled URL even when they appear in natural text with no click intent? (e.g., "see t.co" as part of sentence)
- How to handle branded slugs like "help.redwood" or feature keys without tld? Mark as UNKNOWN and route to product taxonomy?
- Need mapping table from product logs to deterministically map tokens like "sessionId" or "span_id" to USER_ID/OTHER_ID. Could live in Confluence.

Regex cheatsheet (labelers can use in quick search):
- URL-ish: (https?:\/\/)?([\w\-]+\.)+[\w\-]{2,6}([\/:?#].*)?
- SHORT-REDIRECT: ^(t\.co|bit\.ly|tinyurl\.com)\/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$
- EMAIL: [\w.+-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}
- USER_HANDLE: ^@\w[\w\-_.]+$ or ^/u/\w+$
- TIMESTAMP-ISO: \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(T|\s)\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}
